criteria.criterion: Each session phase is started with its own fence settings file: the plan, work and review sessions are not handed the same fence.
criteria.evidence: internal/driver/session.go:150 calls ExtractFence(r.Root, r.Version, s.Phase); extract.go writes <phase>.json from embedded fence/{plan,work,review}.json; session_test.go asserts review.json is passed to --settings

criteria.criterion: The plan fence allows writing .vloop/state/state.json and .vloop/tmp/**; the work and review fences allow writing nothing under .vloop/ but .vloop/tmp/**; all three deny Edit and Write on .git/**.
criteria.evidence: fence/plan.json allows Edit/Write on state.json and .vloop/tmp/**; work.json has bare Edit/Write with denies on .vloop/state, config, defects, interventions, install.json; review.json allows only .vloop/tmp/**; all three deny Edit/Write(.git/**); TestPhaseFenceWrites covers this

criteria.criterion: Every phase fence denies each form F10 lists: git -C . commit, git -c k=v push, git merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, pull, fetch, push to a URL, config, notes, replace, filter-branch, worktree, reflog, gc; find -delete, find -exec, find -fprint; git diff|log|show --output=…; rm -fr and rm -r -f; vloop -C . task set …; vloop brief new.
criteria.evidence: All listed deny rules present in the three fence files; f10Forms in internal/cli/fence_test.go lists each form and TestFenceDeniesBypasses asserts it for every phase (passes)

criteria.criterion: No deny rule of the v0.7.0 fence is dropped or narrowed in any phase fence.
criteria.evidence: Compared git show HEAD:fence/settings.json deny list against each of plan/work/review.json with jq: no old rule missing from any phase

criteria.criterion: internal/cli/fence_test.go holds TestFenceDeniesBypasses, which lists every F10 form and asserts each is denied by every phase fence's deny rules, and lists the allowed commands the skills use and asserts each is still allowed; and TestPhaseFenceWrites, which asserts each phase fence allows and denies the writes above.
criteria.evidence: fence_test.go:70 TestFenceDeniesBypasses (denies plus skillAllowed via judge) and :98 TestPhaseFenceWrites with a per-phase write table; go test ./internal/cli passes

criteria.criterion: TestPluginSkills judges each fenced skill against its own phase's fence and passes; TestEvalGrantsCoverFence checks the eval cases grant at least the work fence's allow list, and the eval cases and docs/guide/evals.md follow it.
criteria.evidence: skills_test.go checkSkillPlugin loads fences per phase via fences[folder]; fenceAllowRules reads readFence("work"); docs/guide/evals.md now cites fence/work.json; work allow list is unchanged so eval grants still cover it; tests pass

criteria.criterion: No skill text changes beyond what F10 requires of the commands it names (brief: Out of scope).
criteria.evidence: git status shows no changes under plugin/ or skills

criteria.criterion: docs/domain/execution/session.md says the fence is advisory, that the driver's checks are the boundary, and that a consumer repository's own .claude/settings.json allow rules also apply to sessions.
criteria.evidence: session.md diff adds 'The fence is advisory.', 'The driver's checks are the boundary', and the consumer-repo .claude/settings.json sentence

notes: The work fence's .vloop/ restriction is a deny list of named subpaths (state, config, defects, interventions, install.json) over a bare Edit/Write, so an unnamed new path under .vloop/ would be writable; acceptable since the fence is declared advisory and later tasks make the driver the boundary.
